table_title: For each landlocked country in Africa, list each bordering country and that bordering country's official language(s).
db_analog: SELECT lc.country, n.country, ol.language FROM countries lc JOIN borders b ON b.country_a = lc.country JOIN countries n ON n.country = b.country_b JOIN official_languages ol ON ol.country = n.country WHERE lc.is_landlocked AND lc.continent = 'Africa' ORDER BY lc.country, n.country, ol.language
temporal_note: Wikidata SPARQL endpoint snapshot, accessed 2026-04-27. Table reflects current Wikidata properties P31 (instance of: landlocked country Q123480), P30 (continent: Africa Q15), P47 (shares border with), and P37 (official language) as of that date. Border and language data may shift as Wikidata is updated (e.g., South African Sign Language was added as South Africa's 12th official language in 2023).
_extraction_notes: Staged via datasets/build_benchmark/sparql_to_csv.py running the SPARQL query at datasets/build_benchmark/sparql_queries/landlocked_africa_neighbor_languages.sparql. The landlocked-country universe clause uses the all-ranks P31 path (`p:P31/ps:P31 wd:Q123480`) rather than the truthy path (`wdt:P31`), so countries whose `instance of: landlocked country` claim is recorded at normal rank rather than preferred rank are still picked up. This yields all 16 commonly listed landlocked African countries (including Rwanda Q1037, whose Q123480 P31 claim is normal-rank). Neighbor and official-language hops keep the truthy `wdt:` path because the canonical preferred-rank classification is what we want for those entities. Composite PK is (Landlocked Country, Bordering Country, Official Language). Result: 225 rows × 3 columns, 0 duplicate PKs.
